# GPU Procurement Guide — November 2026

*Data as of 2026-11-13. All prices in USD per GPU-hour unless noted.*

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The GPU cloud market is in a **tightening phase**. Six-month average on-demand prices have risen 7–35% across most SKUs, driven by power-constrained data center buildouts (Amazon's $5 B in Nvidia servers reportedly sitting idle in warehouses) and sustained AI training demand. Meanwhile, **spot/community-cloud pricing remains 40–66% below on-demand averages**, creating a wide arbitrage window for flexible workloads.

AMD's MI300X/MI325X line is the standout value play right now (382 FLOPS/$), but ecosystem maturity and software support remain the gating factors. NVIDIA's B200/B300 generation is the performance frontier, with B200 at $4.65/hr (Together AI) representing the best new-gen entry point.

**Bottom line:** If you can tolerate preemption, buy spot/community capacity now. If you need 24/7 guaranteed uptime for production inference or long training runs, lock in reserved/committed-use discounts before Q1 2027, when prediction-market pricing implies a 30–50% premium over today's spot rates.

---

## 2. Reserved vs. Spot / On-Demand: Decision Framework

### When to Commit (Reserved / Committed-Use)

| Signal | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Production inference SLA** (p99 latency < 200 ms) | Spot preemption (typically 2-min warning) breaks user-facing latency budgets. |
| **Training runs > 72 h** (e.g., LLM pre-training, fine-tuning > 7 B params) | A mid-run preemption wastes checkpoint I/O and wall-clock time that exceeds the savings. |
| **Multi-node NVLink / NVSwitch topologies** (H100 8-GPU, B200 NVL72) | These are provisioned as fixed clusters; spot pools rarely offer full-node availability. |
| **Regulatory / data-residency constraints** (HIPAA, SOC 2, EU GDPR) | Community-cloud hosts (Vast.ai, some RunPod nodes) may not meet compliance; reserved capacity on CoreWeave, Crusoe, Oracle, or hyperscalers does. |
| **Budget predictability for board/VC reporting** | Committed-use contracts (1-yr, 3-yr) lock a rate 20–40% below on-demand and eliminate variance. |

**Where to lock reserved capacity right now:**

- **CoreWeave** – 1-yr committed H100-SXM at ~$1.50–$1.70/hr (est. 15–25% off their $2.70 on-demand); B200 NVL72 clusters available.
- **Crusoe** – 1-yr A100-80GB at ~$1.70/hr (vs. $2.30 on-demand); B300 at ~$7.50/hr (vs. $8.96).
- **Oracle Cloud (OCI)** – 3-yr reserved B300 at ~$11.00/hr (vs. $15.00 on-demand); strong for regulated workloads.
- **AWS / GCP / Azure** – 1-yr reserved H100-SXM at ~$3.50–$4.00/hr; 3-yr at ~$2.80–$3.20/hr. Less competitive on price but best for integrated data pipelines.

### When to Use Spot / On-Demand / Community Cloud

| Signal | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Batch inference, data labeling, eval sweeps** | Preemption cost is a few minutes of re-queueing; savings of 40–66% dominate. |
| **Experimentation / hyperparameter search** | You can afford to lose a run; parallel spot instances across providers hedge preemption risk. |
| **Short training runs (< 24 h) with frequent checkpoints** | Checkpoint every 30 min; a preemption costs < 10% of run time. |
| **Burst / seasonal workloads** (e.g., holiday inference spikes) | Pay only for what you use; no idle reserved capacity. |
| **Cost-sensitive prototyping** (RTX 4090/5090, L4, T4) | Community-cloud pricing is 50–75% below hyperscaler on-demand. |
